newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt offers stake in contracting firm.
newsitem.headline: Egypt offers stake in contracting firm.

text.p: The Egyptian state's National Company for Construction and Housing on Saturday offered investors 10 percent in its General Upper Egypt Contracting Company at a minimum price of 35 pounds ($10.30) per share.
The firm said in a published announcement that the public offer of at least 30,000 shares, of the firm's total 300,000 shares, would be open to the public from May 20 until May 22.
The announced share price is a so-called "discovery price" and could be increased.
The holding company is also offering 30,000 shares or 10 percent of its stake in General Upper Egypt Contracting Company to the firm's Employee Shareholders' Association.
Individuals must apply for at least 50 shares, while mutual funds and financial firms have a 1,000-share minimum.
Incentives for new shareholders include the dividend per share for the 1996/7 financial year, which General Upper Egypt said would be 3.6 pounds. The financial year ends on June 30.
General Upper Egypt forecast net after-tax profit for 1996/7 to rise to 2.15 million pounds from 2.027 million in 1995/6.
Net sales are expected to jump to 80 million pounds from 68.15 million in 1995/6.
National Bank of Egypt is the agent for the sale.
The share offer is part of Egypt's privatisation-led economic reform programme.
